package org.futo.voiceinput.shared.ggml

import android.os.Build

/**
 * Which Qualcomm chipsets the QNN (Hexagon HTP) voice engine can run on.
 *
 * A QNN graph is compiled for one Hexagon DSP architecture, so a Whisper build
 * only runs on the chipsets Qualcomm published that asset for. The allow-list
 * below is Qualcomm's own, taken from two files rather than guessed:
 *
 *  1. Which chipsets have Whisper assets at all — the release manifest of the
 *     model this engine targets (`precisions[*].chipset_assets` keys):
 *
 *       https://huggingface.co/qualcomm/Whisper-Large-V3-Turbo/raw/main/release_assets.json
 *
 *  2. Which Android SoC part number each chipset slug corresponds to — Qualcomm's
 *     device list, `chipsets[<slug>].aliases` (plus `htp_version` and `soc_model`),
 *     from the same AI Hub Models release:
 *
 *       https://github.com/quic/ai-hub-models/blob/v0.62.2/src/qai_hub_models/devices_and_chipsets.yaml
 *
 * Regenerating both after an upstream release (the second URL's part number is in
 * the `aliases` lists, upper-cased):
 *
 *   V=0.62.2
 *   curl -sSL -o release_assets.json \
 *     https://huggingface.co/qualcomm/Whisper-Large-V3-Turbo/raw/main/release_assets.json
 *   curl -sSL -o devices_and_chipsets.yaml \
 *     https://raw.githubusercontent.com/quic/ai-hub-models/v$V/src/qai_hub_models/devices_and_chipsets.yaml
 *   jq -r '.precisions[].chipset_assets | keys[]' release_assets.json | sort -u
 *
 * The manifest names AI Hub devices, never Android SoC strings, so the mapping to
 * a part number comes from column 2 — with one exception worth spelling out.
 * There is no `qualcomm-snapdragon-8gen2` entry in the manifest; the assets for
 * the Snapdragon 8 Gen 2 — the Galaxy S23 — are published under
 * `qualcomm-qcs8550-proxy`, AI Hub's stand-in device. That it really is the same
 * silicon is Qualcomm's own data: `qualcomm-qcs8550-proxy` and
 * `qualcomm-snapdragon-8gen2` both carry `soc_model: 43`, and the latter lists
 * `sm8550` as an alias with `reference_device: Samsung Galaxy S23`.
 *
 * Chipsets the manifest covers but Android cannot run on are deliberately absent
 * (`snapdragon-x-elite`, `snapdragon-x2-elite`: Windows-on-Snapdragon laptops, so
 * no Android device ever reports them). Chipsets Qualcomm supports on Android but
 * publishes no Whisper assets for are absent by construction — notably Snapdragon
 * 8+ Gen 1 (`sm8475`) and every 7-series — because there would be no model to run.
 *
 * Matching is by part number — [Build.SOC_MODEL] on Android 12+, falling back to
 * [Build.BOARD] / [Build.HARDWARE] for automotive boards that report the part
 * number there instead. Nothing but a part number is accepted, so a ROM that
 * reports only a marketing name or a platform code name is treated as
 * unsupported. That is the safe direction: the QNN option is hidden rather than
 * offered and then failing at load time. (Requiring Android 12+ costs nothing
 * here, since the oldest mobile chipset in the manifest is the 8 Gen 1, which
 * shipped with it.)
 */
object QnnSupport {

    /**
     * One chipset from Qualcomm's Whisper release manifest.
     *
     * @param aiHubId chipset slug, verbatim from the manifest, so the table can be
     *                diffed against it.
     * @param htpVersion Hexagon architecture, from `htp_version` in Qualcomm's
     *                device list. Used to check that this build packaged the
     *                matching `libQnnHtpV<N>Skel.so`.
     * @param socModels values [Build.SOC_MODEL] reports for devices on this
     *                chipset (upper-cased; matched ignoring Qualcomm's `-AB` /
     *                `-AC` / `-AD` part-number suffix).
     */
    private data class SupportedChipset(
        val aiHubId: String,
        val htpVersion: Int,
        val socModels: List<String>
    )

    /**
     * The chipsets with published Whisper-Large-V3-Turbo assets that an Android
     * device can actually be — mobile chipsets first, then automotive/IoT.
     *
     * The automotive/IoT entries only ship a `qnn_context_binary` rather than a
     * `precompiled_qnn_onnx` archive. That single-file kind is recognized by the
     * importer but cannot be loaded by the two-session engine (see
     * `ModelQnnFileFile`), so those entries are listed for completeness of
     * Qualcomm's manifest rather than because a runnable model exists for them
     * today; a device on one is treated as QNN-capable only once a
     * `precompiled_qnn_onnx` archive is assigned.
     */
    private val SUPPORTED_CHIPSETS = listOf(
        SupportedChipset("qualcomm-snapdragon-8gen1", htpVersion = 69, socModels = listOf("SM8450")),
        // AI Hub's stand-in for Snapdragon 8 Gen 2 / SM8550 — see the note above.
        SupportedChipset(
            "qualcomm-qcs8550-proxy",
            htpVersion = 73,
            socModels = listOf("SM8550", "QCS8550")
        ),
        SupportedChipset("qualcomm-snapdragon-8gen3", htpVersion = 75, socModels = listOf("SM8650")),
        SupportedChipset("qualcomm-qcs9075", htpVersion = 73, socModels = listOf("QCS9075")),
        // `sm8750-ac` / `sm8850-ad`: Samsung's SKUs, reported as the base part
        // number once the suffix is stripped.
        SupportedChipset(
            "qualcomm-snapdragon-8-elite-for-galaxy",
            htpVersion = 79,
            socModels = listOf("SM8750")
        ),
        SupportedChipset(
            "qualcomm-snapdragon-8-elite-gen5-for-galaxy",
            htpVersion = 81,
            socModels = listOf("SM8850")
        ),
        SupportedChipset("qualcomm-qcs8275", htpVersion = 75, socModels = listOf("QCS8275")),
        SupportedChipset("qualcomm-sa7255p", htpVersion = 75, socModels = listOf("SA7255P")),
        SupportedChipset("qualcomm-sa8295p", htpVersion = 68, socModels = listOf("SA8295P")),
        SupportedChipset("qualcomm-sa8775p", htpVersion = 73, socModels = listOf("SA8775P"))
    )

    /**
     * Hexagon architecture of the matched chipset (`68`, `69`, `73`, `75`, `79`,
     * `81`), or `null` when the SoC is not one Qualcomm ships Whisper assets for.
     * [BackendSupport] treats a non-null value as "this chipset is supported" and
     * uses the number to confirm the matching `libQnnHtpV<N>Skel.so` made it into
     * this build.
     */
    fun matchedHtpVersion(): Int? = matchedSupportedChipset()?.htpVersion

    private fun matchedSupportedChipset(): SupportedChipset? {
        val candidates = reportedSocModels()
        if (candidates.isEmpty()) return null

        return SUPPORTED_CHIPSETS.firstOrNull { chipset ->
            chipset.socModels.any { it in candidates }
        }
    }

    /**
     * The part numbers this ROM reports, normalised: [Build.SOC_MODEL] first, then
     * [Build.BOARD] / [Build.HARDWARE] as a fallback for automotive boards that
     * report the part number there instead. Qualcomm's device list gives no
     * platform code names, so nothing but a part number is accepted — a device
     * whose ROM reports only a code name is treated as unsupported.
     */
    private fun reportedSocModels(): Set<String> {
        val raw = buildList {
            if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.S) {
                Build.SOC_MODEL?.let { add(it) }
            }
            Build.BOARD?.let { add(it) }
            Build.HARDWARE?.let { add(it) }
        }
        return raw.mapNotNull { normalizeSocModel(it) }.toSet()
    }

    /**
     * Upper-cases a ROM-supplied identifier and strips Qualcomm's part-number
     * suffix (`sm8550-ab` -> `SM8550`). Returns `null` for values that cannot be
     * a part number, so a marketing name such as `"Snapdragon 8 Gen 2"` is not
     * mistaken for one.
     */
    private fun normalizeSocModel(raw: String): String? {
        val normalized = raw.trim().substringBefore('-').uppercase()
        return normalized.takeIf { candidate ->
            candidate.length in 5..8 && candidate.all { it.isLetterOrDigit() }
        }
    }
}

## Deploying the QNN model package

The hardware-acceleration path needs the **`precompiled_qnn_onnx`** model
package (contains the `.onnx` graphs *and* their `_qairt_context.bin`
siblings — the bare `qnn_context_binary` package will **not** work).

Correct package for the S23 Ultra (Snapdragon 8 Gen 2 / SM8550 / HTP v73):

```
REDACTED.zip   (859.8 MB)
```

Deploy it the same way:

```bash
sudo cp <path-to-zip> \
  /var/lib/containers/storage/volumes/syncthing-data/_data/s23/
sudo chown gc:gc \
  /var/lib/containers/storage/volumes/syncthing-data/_data/s23/*.zip
```

Then, **inside the app**: Languages → (locale) → Voice Input → **Import from
file** → select the ZIP. The app extracts `encoder.onnx` + `decoder.onnx`
(+ their context binaries) and registers the model.

## Troubleshooting

**"Files aren't showing up on the phone"**
→ You probably copied them to the host `/var/syncthing/s23` instead of the
volume path. The host path is **not** mounted into the container. Use the
volume path above.

**"File is there but Syncthing isn't syncing"**
→ Check the folder status (step 4). If `state` is stuck, the file may be
`root`-owned — `chown gc:gc` it. If the container isn't running, start it:
`sudo podman start systemd-syncthing`.

**"The ZIP won't import in the app"**
====
| FileKind          | Extension    | Magic (on disk)                                        | Backend        |
|-------------------|--------------|--------------------------------------------------------|----------------|
| `VoiceInput`      | `.bin`       | `ggml` → `0x6c6d6767`                                  | CPU / Vulkan   |
| `VoiceInputQnn`   | `.qnn.bin`   | container header `00 00 00 02 00 00 00 03` (+ build-id) | QNN (Snapdragon) |
| `VoiceInputQnnZip`| `.qnn.zip`   | ZIP (`PK\x03\x04`) containing `encoder.bin` + `decoder.bin` (any nesting) | QNN (Snapdragon) |

### ZIP detection — VERIFIED against the real AI Hub package

The AI Hub `qnn_context_binary` download is a ZIP that nests the model parts
under a top-level directory (`<name>/encoder.bin`, `<name>/decoder.bin`), so
the *first* local entry is a directory, not a model part. `determineFileKind`
scans local file headers (seek-only, no decompression) for any entry whose base
name is `encoder.bin` or `decoder.bin`. Verified against
`REDACTED.zip` —
matches at entry 2 (`…/decoder.bin`).

### Magic detection — VERIFIED against a real context binary

The original assumption (HTP pickle magic at offset 0) was **wrong** and has
been corrected. Verified against the official Qualcomm AI Hub precompiled
`encoder.bin`/`decoder.bin` (`qualcomm-qcs8550-proxy`, qairt 2.45.0):

- **Offset 0** is a **QNN container header**, big-endian: bytes
  `00 00 00 02 00 00 00 03` (container format version `2.3`).
- The HTP *pickle* magics DO exist but sit ~400 KB into the file —
  `Hdr_MAGIC` (LE `0x7309F72B`) at offset 413696, `Hdr_MAGIC_MULTI`
  (LE `0x3790FA5C`) at offset 401408 — unreachable by a 4-byte sniff.
- The SDK **build-id string** `v2.45.0.260326154327` sits at offset ~1852
  (present in the first 4 KB of every context binary).

`determineFileKind` now reads up to 4 KB and classifies a file as
`VoiceInputQnn` when **both** hold:

1. first two big-endian words are `0x00000002` and `0x00000003` (container
   version 2.3), and
2. an embedded `v<digit>.<digit>…` build-id string is present in the header.

This is robust without relying on the proprietary container-body layout.
`Hdr_MAGIC`/`Hdr_MAGIC_MULTI` remain useful as a *body-level* sanity check but
are not used for offset-0 detection.

## Device-type validation (backend routing)

`BackendSupport.resolveBackend(context, preferHardware)` in
`voiceinput-shared/.../ggml/BackendSupport.kt`:

```
preferHardware off  -> CPU
Snapdragon          -> QNN     (Adreno; Vulkan path is known-broken here)
Mali (Exynos/MTK)   -> VULKAN  (Mali untested, not known-broken — selectable for device testing)
Vulkan >= 1.2       -> VULKAN  (whisper.cpp GPU path)
otherwise           -> CPU
```

Snapdragon detection prefers `Build.SOC_MANUFACTURER` (API 31+) containing
`qualcomm`/`qti`, falling back to `ro.hardware`/`ro.product.board` code names
(`msm`, `sdm`, `sm8*`, `kalama`, `pineapple`, …). Mali detection covers
`mediatek`/`samsung`/`exynos`/`mt6*`/`s5e`/`mt8*`/`mt9*`.

A ggml model on a QNN backend (or a QNN backend that is not yet functional)
**falls back to CPU** — ggml cannot run on QNN and QNN cannot run ggml. A QNN
context binary on a non-QNN backend raises `GpuUnavailableException`, which the
recognizer maps to a dedicated `ModelLoadFailure.HardwareUnavailable` message
(`model_load_hw_unavailable`).

## Threading through the call chain

- `VoiceInputAction.loadSettings()` computes `preferHardware`
  (`getVoiceInputModelUseGpu || primaryModel is ModelQnnFileFile`) and resolves
  a `Backend` via `BackendSupport.resolveBackend`.
- `MultiModelRunConfiguration(backend = …)` (was `useGpu: Boolean`).
- `MultiModelRunner` → `ModelManager.obtainModel(model, backend)`, cache key
  `(modelKey, backend)`.
- `ModelLoader.loadGGML(context, backend)`.
- ggml loaders route `VULKAN` → GPU-with-CPU-fallback, everything else → CPU.
- `ModelQnnFileFile.loadGGML` routes `QNN` → `QnnWhisperEngine`, else throws.

## Runtime dependency (when the engine lands)

The QNN HTP runtime needs, on device, `libQnnHtp.so` + `libcdsprpc.so` (the
FastRPC transport) plus the HTP "skel" shared objects. `libcdsprpc.so` is a
system lib on Snapdragon and is declared in the manifest as
`required=false`. Two integration options once a decoder binary exists:

1. **ONNX Runtime QNN EP** — `com.microsoft.onnxruntime:onnxruntime-android-qnn:1.27.0`
   (verified fetchable from Maven Central; 8.0 MB, ships
   `libonnxruntime.so` + `libonnxruntime4j_jni.so`). This is the exact
   version the `whisper-htp-android` reference uses.
   No `libQnnHtp.so` vendoring needed; ORT ships the QNN backend and loads
   the system libraries.

   The QNN runtime itself is pulled separately as
   `com.qualcomm.qti:qnn-runtime:2.48.0` (verified: 68 MB AAR containing
   `libQnnHtp.so`, `libQnnHtpPrepare.so`, `libQnnSystem.so`, `libQnnDsp.so`,
   and the HTP skel/stub pairs for **V66/V68/V69/V73/V75/V79/V81** — V73 is
   the Galaxy S23 Ultra / SM8550 target).

   **Version note:** the precompiled binaries are built with qairt
   **2.45.0.260326154327**, so the runtime must be **≥ 2.45.0**. The reference
   app pins `qnn-runtime:2.48.0` (a 2.45-built context binary loads fine on a
   newer runtime). Do **not** use the local 2.32 SDK's runtime to load these
   binaries — 2.32 < 2.45 and will reject them.
2. **Direct QNN C API** — vendored `libQnnHtp.so` + `libQnnSystem.so` +
   skels, load `libcdsprpc.so` via `System.loadLibrary`, and call
   `QnnContext_createFromBinary`. More control (matches how
   `whisper-htp-android` works) but more build work.

to `SAMPLES_30S` (480 000 samples / 3000 mel frames) and the encoder input tensor

content.text:
The logs pinpoint the regression: switching from Chinese to French tried to load a **second ~1 GB QNN model while the Chinese one was still cached**. That exhausts the HTP/DSP resources; the load fails, and then every later load fails until reboot. All three QNN ZIPs are byte-identical anyway — language is selected by prompt token, not by weights.

I’m fixing it so QNN uses **one shared engine** across locales instead of one per language.

package org.futo.voiceinput.shared.ggml

import android.content.Context
import android.system.Os
import android.util.Log
import android.util.Base64
import androidx.annotation.Keep
import kotlinx.coroutines.withContext
import org.json.JSONArray
import java.io.ByteArrayOutputStream
import java.io.File

/**
 * Qualcomm QNN (Hexagon HTP / NPU) engine.
 *
 * Runs Qualcomm AI Hub's precompiled Whisper-Large-V3-Turbo-Quantized (w8a16)
 * context binaries through ONNX Runtime's QNN Execution Provider. The native
 * side (libvoiceinput_qnn.so) holds the mel front end, the ORT sessions and a
 * fixed-shape KV-cache greedy decode loop (see native/jni/src/qnn-htp/).
 *
 * The model is a single-shot 30-second window (not the streaming VAD loop the
 * CPU engine uses): the mel front end pads/truncates its PCM to 30 s, runs
 * encoder + a greedy decode seeded with the prompt, and detokenizes the result.
 *
 * Because that window is a hard limit of the precompiled graph, [infer] decodes
 * long recordings in 29 s chunks with a 5 s overlap and de-duplicates the
 * overlapping text (see [LongFormChunking]); everything past 30 s used to be
 * dropped silently.
 */
@Keep
class QnnWhisperEngine(
    context: Context,
    private val encoderOnnxFile: File,
    private val decoderOnnxFile: File
) : WhisperEngine {

    companion object {
        private const val VARIANT_TURBO_W8A16 = 2
        private const val MEL_BINS = 128

        /**
         * Long-form chunking. Mirrors [LongFormChunking]'s defaults: the graph
         * only accepts 30 s of mel, so decode 29 s at a time and overlap by 5 s
         * to keep words on the boundary intact.
         */
        private const val CHUNK_SAMPLES = LongFormChunking.DEFAULT_CHUNK_SAMPLES
        private const val OVERLAP_SAMPLES = LongFormChunking.DEFAULT_OVERLAP_SAMPLES

        // Whisper large-v3 vocab special tokens (DIFFER from the v2/small ids).
        private const val SOT = 50258            // <|startoftranscript|>
        private const val TRANSCRIBE = 50360     // <|transcribe|>
        private const val NOTIMESTAMPS = 50364   // <|notimestamps|>
        private const val LANG_FIRST = 50259     // <|en|>; 100 language tokens follow
        /** Prompt sentinel: the native decoder detects the language from <|sot|> logits. */
        private const val AUTO_DETECT_LANGUAGE = -1
        // <|endoftext|>: the first control token. BPE *content* tokens are
        // 0..EOT-1, so only those are eligible for the decoder prompt.
        private const val EOT = 50257

        // ISO 639-1 code -> index into the whisper language-token block
        // (token id = LANG_FIRST + index). Order matches whisper.cpp g_lang.
        private val LANG_INDEX: Map<String, Int> = mapOf(
            "en" to 0, "zh" to 1, "de" to 2, "es" to 3, "ru" to 4, "ko" to 5,
            "fr" to 6, "ja" to 7, "pt" to 8, "tr" to 9, "pl" to 10, "ca" to 11,
            "nl" to 12, "ar" to 13, "sv" to 14, "it" to 15, "id" to 16, "hi" to 17,
            "fi" to 18, "vi" to 19, "he" to 20, "uk" to 21, "el" to 22, "ms" to 23,
            "cs" to 24, "ro" to 25, "da" to 26, "hu" to 27, "ta" to 28, "no" to 29,
            "th" to 30, "ur" to 31, "hr" to 32, "bg" to 33, "lt" to 34, "la" to 35,
            "mi" to 36, "ml" to 37, "cy" to 38, "sk" to 39, "te" to 40, "fa" to 41,
            "lv" to 42, "bn" to 43, "sr" to 44, "az" to 45, "sl" to 46, "kn" to 47,
            "et" to 48, "mk" to 49, "br" to 50, "eu" to 51, "is" to 52, "hy" to 53,
            "ne" to 54, "mn" to 55, "bs" to 56, "kk" to 57, "sq" to 58, "sw" to 59,
            "gl" to 60, "mr" to 61, "pa" to 62, "si" to 63, "km" to 64, "sn" to 65,
            "yo" to 66, "so" to 67, "af" to 68, "oc" to 69, "ka" to 70, "be" to 71,
            "tg" to 72, "sd" to 73, "gu" to 74, "am" to 75, "yi" to 76, "lo" to 77,
            "uz" to 78, "fo" to 79, "ht" to 80, "ps" to 81, "tk" to 82, "nn" to 83,
            "mt" to 84, "sa" to 85, "lb" to 86, "my" to 87, "bo" to 88, "tl" to 89,
            "mg" to 90, "as" to 91, "tt" to 92, "haw" to 93, "ln" to 94, "ha" to 95,
            "ba" to 96, "jw" to 97, "su" to 98, "yue" to 99
        )

        init {
            System.loadLibrary("voiceinput_qnn")
        }
    }

    private var handle: Long = 0L
    @Volatile private var cancelled = false
    private var partialResultCallback: (String) -> Unit = { }

    // Whisper large-v3-turbo detokenizer vocab (base64 UTF-8 bytes per id).
    private val vocab: Array<ByteArray>

    private class PromptVocab(val byText: Map<String, Int>, val maxBytes: Int)

    /**
     * Byte-level BPE vocabulary as ISO-8859-1 strings (1 char per byte), so the
     * initial prompt / glossary can be tokenized by greedy longest match. Only
     * content tokens (`id < EOT`) are indexed, so a control token can never be
     * emitted into the decoder prompt. Built lazily: the CPU path never uses it.
     */
    private val promptVocab: PromptVocab by lazy {
        val byText = HashMap<String, Int>()
        var maxBytes = 0
        for (id in 0 until minOf(EOT, vocab.size)) {
            val bytes = vocab[id]
            if (bytes.isEmpty()) continue
            val key = String(bytes, Charsets.ISO_8859_1)
            if (byText.putIfAbsent(key, id) == null) maxBytes = maxOf(maxBytes, bytes.size)
        }

The reference model shows the same sensitivity: adding the app’s Latin-script glossary (`Émile, Blaise…`) to a Chinese decode corrupts it badly. For the QNN model it goes further and emits `endoftext`. The glossary is a strong language/script prior and should never be fed to a CJK decode.

I’m making QNN skip the dictionary prompt for CJK targets, then retesting.

package org.futo.voiceinput.shared.ggml

import android.content.Context
import android.system.Os
import android.util.Log
import android.util.Base64
import androidx.annotation.Keep
import kotlinx.coroutines.withContext
import org.json.JSONArray
import java.io.ByteArrayOutputStream
import java.io.File
import java.io.FileOutputStream
import kotlin.math.abs
import kotlin.math.max
import kotlin.math.sqrt

/**
 * Qualcomm QNN (Hexagon HTP / NPU) engine.
 *
 * Runs Qualcomm AI Hub's precompiled Whisper-Large-V3-Turbo-Quantized (w8a16)
 * context binaries through ONNX Runtime's QNN Execution Provider. The native
 * side (libvoiceinput_qnn.so) holds the mel front end, the ORT sessions and a
 * fixed-shape KV-cache greedy decode loop (see native/jni/src/qnn-htp/).
 *
 * The model is a single-shot 30-second window (not the streaming VAD loop the
 * CPU engine uses): the mel front end pads/truncates its PCM to 30 s, runs
 * encoder + a greedy decode seeded with the prompt, and detokenizes the result.
 *
 * Because that window is a hard limit of the precompiled graph, [infer] decodes
 * long recordings in 29 s chunks with a 5 s overlap and de-duplicates the
 * overlapping text (see [LongFormChunking]); everything past 30 s used to be
 * dropped silently.
 */
@Keep
class QnnWhisperEngine(
    context: Context,
    private val encoderOnnxFile: File,
    private val decoderOnnxFile: File
) : WhisperEngine {

    private val appContext = context.applicationContext

    companion object {
        private const val VARIANT_TURBO_W8A16 = 2
        private const val MEL_BINS = 128

        /**
         * Long-form chunking. Mirrors [LongFormChunking]'s defaults: the graph
         * only accepts 30 s of mel, so decode 29 s at a time and overlap by 5 s
         * to keep words on the boundary intact.
         */
        private const val CHUNK_SAMPLES = LongFormChunking.DEFAULT_CHUNK_SAMPLES
        private const val OVERLAP_SAMPLES = LongFormChunking.DEFAULT_OVERLAP_SAMPLES

        // Whisper large-v3 vocab special tokens (DIFFER from the v2/small ids).
        private const val SOT = 50258            // <|startoftranscript|>
        private const val TRANSCRIBE = 50360     // <|transcribe|>
        private const val NOTIMESTAMPS = 50364   // <|notimestamps|>
        private const val LANG_FIRST = 50259     // <|en|>; 100 language tokens follow
        /** Languages whose script is incompatible with the Latin-script glossary prompt. */
        private val CJK_LANGUAGES = setOf("zh", "ja", "ko", "yue")
        /** Prompt sentinel: the native decoder detects the language from <|sot|> logits. */
        private const val AUTO_DETECT_LANGUAGE = -1
        // <|endoftext|>: the first control token. BPE *content* tokens are
        // 0..EOT-1, so only those are eligible for the decoder prompt.
        private const val EOT = 50257

        // ISO 639-1 code -> index into the whisper language-token block

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Wireless ADB helper for manual on-device validation.
#
# Phone setup (Android 11+):
#   1. Settings -> About phone -> tap "Build number" 7 times.
#   2. Settings -> System -> Developer options -> Wireless debugging -> On.
#   3. Tap "Pair device with pairing code"; keep that dialog open.
#   4. On the Wireless debugging screen note the *connect* IP:port.
#
# Usage:
#   tools/phone-debug.sh discover
#   tools/phone-debug.sh pair 192.168.4.50:41234 123456
#   tools/phone-debug.sh connect 192.168.4.50:37123
#   tools/phone-debug.sh devices
#   tools/phone-debug.sh install [apk]
#   tools/phone-debug.sh log [seconds] [output-file]
#
# Pairing and connect ports are different; both are shown on the phone.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
ANDROID_HOME="${ANDROID_HOME:-/var/lib/aoe/android-sdk}"
ADB="${ADB:-$ANDROID_HOME/platform-tools/adb}"
APK="${APK:-$ROOT/build/outputs/apk/unstable/debug/lithuanians-unstable-debug.apk}"
PACKAGE="${PACKAGE:-org.futo.inputmethod.latin.unstable}"

if [[ ! -x "$ADB" ]]; then
    echo "adb not found at $ADB (set ADB=... or ANDROID_HOME=...)" >&2
    exit 1
fi

usage() {
    sed -n '2,18p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'
}

cmd="${1:-help}"
shift || true

case "$cmd" in
    discover)
        "$ADB" mdns services
        ;;

    pair)
        address="${1:-}"
        code="${2:-}"
        if [[ -z "$address" ]]; then
            echo "usage: $0 pair <ip:pairing-port> [code]" >&2
            exit 2
        fi
        if [[ -n "$code" ]]; then
            printf '%s\n' "$code" | "$ADB" pair "$address"
        else
            "$ADB" pair "$address"
        fi
        ;;

    connect)
        address="${1:-}"
        if [[ -z "$address" ]]; then
            echo "usage: $0 connect <ip:connect-port>" >&2
            exit 2
        fi
        "$ADB" connect "$address"
        "$ADB" devices -l
        ;;

    devices)
        "$ADB" devices -l
        ;;

    install)
        apk="${1:-$APK}"
        if [[ ! -f "$apk" ]]; then
            echo "APK not found: $apk" >&2
            exit 1
        fi
        echo "Installing $apk"
        "$ADB" install -r -d -g "$apk"
        echo "Launching $PACKAGE"

content.text:
Fixed and published.

**Root cause:** the QNN w8a16 decoder was being seeded with the personal-dictionary glossary as an “initial prompt.” It treated that as a completed previous transcript and emitted `<|endoftext|>` immediately:

- Chinese: **every** attempt failed.
- English/French: roughly **half** failed.
- The same audio transcribed fine with full-precision reference Whisper, so it was QNN-specific.

**Changes:**
- QNN now builds only `<|sot|> + language + <|transcribe|> + <|notimestamps|>` — **no glossary prompt**. CPU/Vulkan still use the glossary.
- One shared QNN engine across locales, preventing the “second model wedges the DSP” failure.
- Model selection now prefers the current locale’s imported model.

**Validated:** 11 consecutive attempts across English, French, and Chinese — zero empty transcripts, zero QNN errors.

**APK published to Syncthing:** `lithuanians-unstable-debug.apk`
- Size: `247,731,552`
- SHA-256: `1210d6fd82825ff8ae053c3b64297f21ef43426472cdd850fe2da56f8654b6b5`

One tradeoff: QNN no longer gets dictionary spelling hints. If you want those back on QNN, it should be done as post-processing rather than an initial prompt.

I think it's fair enough. There is only one model for all languages for QNN. I think that's okay because typically we will be able to load larger models that are multi-langual. The only thing we need to make sure the UI reflects that so the people can decide when they load QNN model that is going to be shared across all languages. We need to ensure that is very visible from a UI perspective.

data class InputLanguage(
    val tag: String,
    val name: String,
    val inputMethodSubtype: InputMethodSubtype
)

fun getActiveLanguages(context: Context): List<InputLanguage> {
    SubtypeLocaleUtils.init(context)
    return context.getSettingBlocking(SubtypesSetting)
        .let { Subtypes.layoutsMappedByLanguage(it) }
        .map {
        InputLanguage(
            it.value.first().locale,
            Subtypes.getName(it.value.first()),
            it.value.first()
        )
    }
}


fun FileKind.preferenceKeyFor(locale: String): Preferences.Key<String> {
    assert(this != FileKind.Invalid)
    val locale = locale.replace("#", "H")
    return stringPreferencesKey("resource_${name}_${locale}")
}

fun FileKind.namePreferenceKeyFor(locale: String): Preferences.Key<String> {
    assert(this != FileKind.Invalid)
    val locale = locale.replace("#", "H")
    return stringPreferencesKey("resourcename_${name}_${locale}")
}

/**

 * [backendPreferenceKeyFor]; still read once so existing installs keep their

fun FileKind.gpuPreferenceKeyFor(locale: String): Preferences.Key<Boolean> {
    assert(this != FileKind.Invalid)
    val locale = locale.replace("#", "H")
    return booleanPreferencesKey("resource_${name}_gpu_${locale}")
}

/** Per-locale, explicitly chosen [Backend] for the assigned voice input model. */
fun FileKind.backendPreferenceKeyFor(locale: String): Preferences.Key<String> {

    return stringPreferencesKey("resource_${name}_backend_${locale}")

content.text:
Implemented the shared-QNN model UX and storage.

### What changed

- **QNN ZIP is now stored once, globally**
  - New synthetic key: `QNN_SHARED_RESOURCE_KEY = "qnn-shared"` in `ImportResourceActivity.kt`.
  - `ResourceHelper.findSharedQnnVoiceInputModel()` resolves that one model for every language.
  - Existing per-locale QNN ZIPs still load, but are cleaned up when a shared model is imported or removed.

- **Import screen is explicit**
  - QNN ZIP imports no longer ask “which language?”
  - Shows a prominent notice that one QNN model is shared by every language.
  - Single action: **“Install QNN model for all languages”**.

- **Languages screen shows a banner**
  - While a shared QNN ZIP is installed, the top of **Languages & Models** shows:
    - “One Qualcomm (QNN) model is installed and shared across all languages.”

- **Model confirmation dialog**
  - QNN ZIP dialog explains that replacing/removing it affects every language.
  - “Remove” now deletes the shared QNN model for all languages.
  - Legacy per-locale QNN ZIPs remain removable.

### Build / delivery

- Commit: `b3ffc28d5` — *Make the shared QNN model explicit and install it once for all languages*
- APK: `/var/lib/aoe/syncthing/s23/lithuanians-unstable-debug.apk`
- Size: `249,090,090` bytes
- SHA-256: `fb6159d9970635a4705ea90d65050706737c1653c5d8403efff89e931b17c405`

I could not re-run the on-device UI/transcription validation because wireless ADB is currently refusing connections (`192.168.4.25:5555`). The APK is synced to the phone and ready to install. ## Outcome

The tree was reviewed in depth, verified to build via the distrobox android-dbx build script, two small cleanups were made (.gitignore for .pi/, orphaned KDoc in ImportResourceActivity.kt), and all work was committed as a single 'Voice input: per-language backend picker + QNN/Vulkan hardening' commit. The actual push to GitHub (and identification of the additional repo) was not completed before the transcript ended.

## Learnings

### Repository

- Main repo is /home/gc/android-keyboard on branch master, with side branches GPUEnablement and PartialTranscription.
- The ‘libs‘ submodule tracks oozut/android-libs (pinned commit f71fba92) and supplies the ONNX Runtime QNN and QNN runtime AARs.
- ResourceHelper.resolveVoiceInputSelection() is the single source of truth for model+backend selection, replacing the old boolean hardware-acceleration switch.
- QNN routing is driven by ModelLoader.requiredBackend rather than special-casing ModelQnnFileFile.
- QnnSupport uses an allow-list of Snapdragon chipsets (HTP version + SOC_MODEL) rather than a blanket Qualcomm check.
- .pi/ is a local agent scratch directory (build.log, launch.log, extensions) that should not be committed; .entire/ holds session checkpoints/metadata used for local context recovery.
- Untracked docs (BUILDING.md, DEPLOYMENT.md, GPU_REVIEW_RECOMMENDATIONS.md, PARTIAL_TRANSCRIPTION_PLAN.md) and GPU_QNN_INTEGRATION.md changes were part of the pending work.

### Code

- `voiceinput-shared/src/main/java/org/futo/voiceinput/shared/ggml/QnnSupport.kt` — New file implementing Snapdragon chipset allow-list (HTP version + SOC_MODEL) and a Vulkan gate mirroring ggml-vulkan requirements; no longer blacklists Mali.
- `voiceinput-shared/src/main/java/org/futo/voiceinput/shared/ggml/BackendSupport.kt` — Defines the Backend enum (CPU/Vulkan/QNN) and availability/unavailableReason logic used by both the settings UI and the voice input action.
- `voiceinput-shared/src/main/java/org/futo/voiceinput/shared/whisper/ModelManager.kt` — Switched to ConcurrentHashMap + computeIfAbsent so parallel preloads of models are safe.
- `voiceinput-shared/src/main/java/org/futo/voiceinput/shared/ggml/QnnWhisperEngine.kt` — Tokenizes the personal-dictionary glossary into the decoder prompt, restricted to content tokens (id < EOT) to avoid the endoftext-first-token failure.
- `native/jni/src/whisper-gpu/org_futo_voiceinput_WhisperGGMLGpu.cpp` — Introduced a process-global ggml log router with a live-state registry, fixing a use-after-free after close() and a leaked decoder output on failure; JNI local refs are now released.
- `native/jni/src/qnn-htp/whisper_mel.cpp` — Filterbank initialization is now serialized to avoid concurrent-init races.
- `java/src/org/futo/inputmethod/latin/uix/ImportResourceActivity.kt` — Non-QNN-ZIP import failures now show a generic error message; an orphaned KDoc was cleaned up during review.
- `java/src/org/futo/inputmethod/latin/uix/settings/pages/Languages.kt` — Reworked to expose the per-language CPU/Vulkan/QNN backend picker instead of the old hw-accel toggle, with strings like voice_input_backend_* and QNN unavailability messaging.

result.output:
Attach an existing agent session that wasn't captured by hooks.

This creates a checkpoint from the session's transcript and links it to the
last commit, or to the commit named by --commit. Use this when hooks failed
to fire or weren't installed when the session started, or to attach a
research session.

How the session is linked follows from two facts about the commit — does it
already have a checkpoint, and is it pushed — the same for HEAD and --commit:
  - It already has a checkpoint: the session is added to it. Git history is
    not changed.
  - It is already pushed: the commit is left unchanged and the link is
    recorded in a new checkpoint, which is pushed right away. The link counts
    once the commit's author attaches it, and names that exact commit: after
    a rebase or amend, attach the session to the new commit.
  - It isn't pushed: the Entire-Checkpoint trailer is added to it, which
    rewrites it and any commits after it on the current branch (their content
    is unchanged). A trailer survives a later rebase. Merges after the commit,
    or a rebase or merge in progress, are refused. If a remote can't be
    reached to confirm the commit isn't pushed, attach refuses rather than
    risk rewriting a shared commit.

attach prints what it is about to do and asks before doing it. Without a
terminal (an agent or a script) it changes nothing and exits non-zero; show
the user what it printed, and once they agree, rerun with --force.

A session can be attached to more than one commit. Each checkpoint records the
turns since the session's previous checkpoint.

Use --review to tag the attached session as an agent review. The
first user prompt in the transcript is recorded as the review prompt.
Pass --skills to declare which skills were actually run; omit to
attach a review without a declared skills list.

Works with any registered agent, including external agents enabled via
external_agents in .entire/settings.local.json (that file only, and only
when it is untracked). Run 'entire agent list' to see the full list.

If --agent doesn't locate a transcript, Entire auto-detects the agent from
the transcript and prints the detected agent name.

Usage:
  entire session attach <session-id> [flags]

Flags:
  -a, --agent string     Agent that created the session (see 'entire agent list' for registered agents, including external) (default "claude-code")
      --commit string    Link the session to this commit (hash, ref, or HEAD~n) instead of the last one
  -f, --force            Skip the confirmation. Only after the user has agreed to what attach describes
  -h, --help             help for attach
      --review           Tag the attached session as an agent review
      --skills strings   Optional: declare which review skills were run in this session. Only used with --review
